entries.english: Kisii (Kossova) Northward Migration into the Kitoto Plain & the Pure-Bred Kisii Origin of Chief Kitoto of the Nyamoga Clan
entries.translation: Chief Kitoto of the Kitoto plain (head of the Nyamoga / Moga clan of Kanu/Kadibo): although wearing Nilotic ornaments and married to Ja-Luo wives, he is a pure-bred native of the Kisii (Kossova) nation whose bands trekked northward along the 10-mile lake corridor below the 2,000-ft Nandi escarpment; Kisii oral tradition also records an ancestral migration from the southward / Kilimanjaro region

entries.english: Six Noun Plural Classes of Bantu Kisii or Kossova (Classes I–VI) in Hobley (1902, p. 86)
entries.translation: Class I (um- → aw-): umuntu → awantu ('man/person → people') • Class II (o- → mi-; [m]u- → [m]i-): okuwoko → mikowoko ('arm → arms'), (m)umogwe → (m)imegwe ('arrow → arrows') • Class III (invariant in plural): muriro ('fire') • Class IV (iki-/ichi- → ivi-): ikisiri → ivisiri ('axe → axes'), ichiara → iviara ('finger → fingers') • Class V (u- → ama-; li-/ili- → ma-; [li]ki- → mi-; [l]e- → ama-): uwusio → amasio ('face'), liliga → amaliga ('tear'), (li)kisimba → misimba ('cat'), (l)erino → amaino ('ivory/tooth') • Class VI (e-/i- → chi-/achi-; e- → si-): imbandi → chimbandi ('ground-nut'), enjoka → chinjoka ('snake'), enzwi → sinzwi ('fish')

entries.english: Kossova (Kisii) Personal Pronouns, Demonstratives, Possessives & Adjectives in Hobley (1902, Ch. VII § I, pp. 90–91)
entries.translation: Pronouns: ninchi ('I/me'), nururi ('thou'), nururio ('he'), nitwi ('we'), ninwi ('you'), embabu ('they'); wonzi, twenzi, vionzi ('all') • Demonstratives & Possessives: muntuuiga ('this man') / muntuulia ('that man'), umutiuiga ('this tree') / umutiulia ('that tree'), aiga ('here') / alia ('there'); inyumbaane ('my house'), inyumbayako ('thy house'), inyumbayake ('his house'), umuchi wetu ('our town'), seno ('your country'), awana wawo ('their children') • Adjectives: umuvi / kivi ('bad person / thing'), ichia ('good/nice'), umuke / ageki ('great'), kisinini ('little'), mulafu ('white'), umumwamu ('black'), chining ('plenty'), tindi ('no/not')
